chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar al-Alawi al-Samarqandi (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, saying: Muhammad ibn Nasir told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa told us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Ayub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (Allah's blessings be upon him)
regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'So they did not yield to their Lord, nor did they humbly supplicate'
He said: Tadharru' (humble supplication) is raising the hands.

key_terms.التَّضَرُّعُ: Humble supplication or submission, specifically defined here as raising hands
key_terms.رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ: Raising the hands (a ritual gesture in prayer or supplication)
key_terms.فَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا: So they did not yield/subdue themselves

ai.seo_question: What is the physical meaning of 'tadharru'' in Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a specific exegetical definition for 'tadharru'' as the physical act of raising hands, distinguishing it from general supplication. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on linking internal spiritual humility with external ritual gestures, a concept further supported by the Prophet's practice of raising hands during du'a. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the etiquette of bodily movement in prayer and supplication within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition.
